name: French Breakfast Puffs
desc: Tender nutmeg muffins rolled in melted butter and cinnamon sugar while hot.

source.title: French Breakfast Puffs
source.evidence: Same shortening, sugar, egg, 1 1/2 cups flour, baking powder, nutmeg and milk batter, baked at 350°F and rolled in 1/2 cup melted butter and 1/2 cup cinnamon sugar; Betty Crocker uses 1/2 tsp salt and fills 15 cups.

steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Coat 9 cups of a standard muffin tin with cooking spray.
Beat the shortening, 1/2 cup sugar, and egg with a mixer until smooth.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg together. Add to the shortening mixture in three additions, alternating with the milk, mixing until no dry flour remains.
Fill the muffin cups two-thirds full. Bake until golden brown and a toothpick in the center comes out clean, 20 to 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, combine the cinnamon and 1/2 cup sugar in a shallow bowl and put the melted butter in another.
Cool the muffins in the pan 2 minutes, then while still hot roll each one in the butter, then in the cinnamon sugar. Serve warm.
tips: Betty Crocker spreads the same batter across 15 muffin cups for smaller puffs and uses 1/2 tsp salt; start checking those at 20 minutes.

references.title: French Breakfast Puffs
references.usedFor: golden brown doneness cue, 15-cup alternative, salt difference
